extracted.intended_audience: editors, anthology compilers, literary critics, and short-story writers (American short fiction)
extracted.subtask_short: anthology selection of American short stories
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for selecting and ranking short stories for an annual anthology/yearbook of American short fiction, including selection method, quality tests, grouping/marking, and publication constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test of Substance
rubrics_metrics.description: The first test of a short story is to report upon how vitally compelling the writer makes his selected facts or incidents; this test may be known as the test of substance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substance is achieved by the artist in creation: a fact or group of facts only obtain substantial embodiment when the artist's power of compelling imaginative persuasion transforms them into a living truth. The selector should ask how vitally convincing the chosen material is as rendered by the writer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test of Form
rubrics_metrics.description: The true artist will seek to shape this living substance into the most beautiful and satisfying form by skilful selection and arrangement of his material and by the most direct and appealing presentation of it in portrayal and characterization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation of form focuses on selection, arrangement, presentation, portrayal, and characterization — i.e., how well the material is shaped into an aesthetically satisfying story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double standard: substance AND form
rubrics_metrics.description: Each story is tested by the double standard of substance and form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection is not one-dimensional: a story may survive substance or form alone, but the highest ranking requires success on both tests. The editor explicitly uses both tests in impartial evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organic substance (avoid inorganic fiction)
rubrics_metrics.description: No substance is of importance in fiction, unless it is organic substance, that is to say, substance in which the pulse of life is beating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid 'inorganic' fiction — stories that lack living, organic substance. Prefer works where life and psychological/imaginative reality are manifest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compelling imaginative persuasion (how facts become living truth)
rubrics_metrics.description: Facts or incidents in a story only obtain substantial embodiment when the artist's power of compelling imaginative persuasion transforms them into a living truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessors should look for the writer's ability to transform material into imaginative reality rather than mere reportage or bare facts; this is central to the substance test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection method: impartial, surrender to writer's point of view
rubrics_metrics.description: Take each short story by itself and examine it impartially; surrender oneself to the writer's point of view and, granting his choice of material and personal interpretation, test it by substance and form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The selector should grant the writer's chosen perspective and evaluate how well that perspective is realized, rather than judge by preconceived personal preferences or external formulas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-pattern: avoid formulaic or dogmatic criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor is not interested in formulae; organized criticism at its best would be nothing more than dead criticism, as all dogmatic interpretation of life is always dead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid rigid, rule-bound approaches that reduce stories to checklists; value living, flexible critical judgement attentive to imaginative reality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping / asterisk marking system
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories fall into four groups indicated in the year-book index by zero, one, two, or three asterisks: none (fail tests), one asterisk (survive either substance or form), two asterisks (survive both tests), three asterisks (highest distinction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the asterisk system to communicate levels of distinction: no mark = fails to survive either test; * = survives one; ** = survives both and may deserve a second reading; *** = unites genuine substance and artistic form and may merit republication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second-reading criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories of still greater distinction include narratives which may lay convincing claim to a second reading because each has survived both tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A marker of quality is whether the story rewards or invites a second reading — an indicator used to separate two-asterisk stories from lesser ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highest distinction: unity of substance and artistic form
rubrics_metrics.description: A small group of stories unite genuine substance and artistic form in a closely woven pattern with such sincerity that these stories may fairly claim a position in our literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These three-asterisk stories are the anthology's elite — selected for republication and treated as the year's most enduring short fiction; selection here implies literary rather than merely technical excellence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope restriction: American originals only (no English stories or translations)
rubrics_metrics.description: It has been a point of honor with me not to republish an English story, nor a translation from a foreign author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The anthology/compiler limits inclusion to original American short stories; translations and non‑American original works are excluded from selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: One story per author rule
rubrics_metrics.description: I have also made it a rule not to include more than one story by an individual author in the volume.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To maximize breadth and representation, avoid including multiple pieces by the same author in a single annual volume.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended length and payment limits to raise standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Except in an unusual instance, the short story should be limited to five thousand words, and the compensation for it should not exceed three hundred dollars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are prescriptive recommendations (addressed to magazine editors) intended to combat wordiness and commercial standardization and to encourage imaginative writers rather than commercial exploiters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement does not imply ranking
rubrics_metrics.description: The order in which the stories in this volume are printed is not intended as an indication of their comparative excellence; the arrangement is alphabetical by authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers and reviewers should not infer comparative merit from the sequence of the anthology; alphabetical order is neutral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial aim: chronicle first signs of grace and render best work accessible
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor's essential function is to begin at the bottom and record the first signs of grace rather than to limit himself to the top; to chronicle work which renders life imaginatively in organic substance and artistic form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An anthology's curatorial mission can be to discover and make accessible significant work that might otherwise be buried in commonplaceness, not only to celebrate already-established masterpieces.
